_comment: Chain definition for project-genesis-chain. Greenfield flow from product idea to release-ready local repository using existing specialist skills where possible.
description: Greenfield project creation: intake -> constitution -> product spec -> clarification -> architecture -> tasks -> bootstrap -> first slice -> verification -> hardening -> release prep

phases.name: Step 0 - Establish project intent, scope, and execution mode
phases.reason: Capture project name, target directory, product goal, users, constraints, stack preferences, execution mode, and approval boundaries before creating artifacts.
phases.query_suffix: Create a concise project intake brief. Include project name, target path, product goal, primary users, non-goals, stack preferences, constraints, execution mode, approvals needed, and open questions. Do not create source files in the target project yet.

phases.name: Step 1 - Create project constitution
phases.reason: Create governing principles for quality, architecture, tests, UX, security, release discipline, and skill routing.

phases.name: Step 2a - Generate epics and user stories
phases.reason: Convert the product idea and constitution into structured epics, user stories, technical contracts, and traceability notes.

phases.name: Step 2b - Draft testable acceptance criteria
phases.reason: Turn the highest-priority stories into testable acceptance criteria with explicit assumptions and coverage gaps.

phases.name: Step 3 - Analyze requirement testability and ambiguity
phases.reason: Review the draft requirements and criteria for ambiguity, missing NFRs, testability gaps, and delivery risks before architecture planning.
phases._hitl_note: Gate before architecture. Human should answer blocking questions or approve proceeding with documented assumptions.

phases.name: Step 4 - Create greenfield architecture plan
phases.reason: Select architecture, stack, boundaries, data model, API contracts, UI architecture, deployment shape, security posture, and validation strategy.

phases.name: Step 5 - Create implementation task plan
phases.reason: Convert approved specification and architecture into ordered tasks with dependencies, test-first steps, file targets, validation commands, and skill-routing hints.
phases._hitl_note: Gate before repository bootstrap and implementation. Human approves the plan, target path, and install/network actions.

phases.name: Step 6 - Bootstrap repository skeleton
phases.reason: Create the repository skeleton using stack-specific bootstrap skills when available, plus common docs, environment samples, and validation scaffolding.

phases.name: Step 7 - Implement first vertical slice
phases.reason: Implement the approved first vertical slice using the bootstrapped repository, acceptance criteria, and implementation tasks.
phases.query_suffix: Treat this as the first approved feature in a newly bootstrapped repository. Implement only the first independently demonstrable vertical slice from the task plan. Keep source, tests, docs, and traceability aligned.

phases.name: Step 8a - Unit and component validation
phases.reason: Run or add the repository-native unit and component tests for the implemented slice.

phases.name: Step 8b - API and service contract validation
phases.reason: Validate API contracts and service behavior when the architecture exposes REST, HTTP, event, or service boundaries.
phases.query_suffix: If the bootstrapped project has no API or service boundary yet, state exactly: 'api contract validation: not applicable for this slice' and stop.

phases.name: Step 8c - Browser or end-to-end validation
phases.reason: Implement or run browser-level validation for user-facing flows when the project has a UI.
phases.query_suffix: If the bootstrapped project has no browser UI yet, state exactly: 'e2e validation: not applicable for this slice' and stop.

phases.name: Step 8d - Responsive validation
phases.reason: Validate responsive behavior for UI surfaces across the smallest useful viewport matrix.
phases.query_suffix: If the project has no responsive UI surface yet, state exactly: 'responsive validation: not applicable for this slice' and stop.

phases.name: Step 8e - Accessibility validation
phases.reason: Audit accessibility for UI surfaces introduced by the first slice.
phases.query_suffix: If the project has no user-facing UI yet, state exactly: 'accessibility validation: not applicable for this slice' and stop.

phases.name: Step 9 - Review automation quality and evidence
phases.reason: Review test evidence, coverage quality, gaps, and false-confidence risks across all validation phases.

phases.name: Step 10 - Principal hardening audit
phases.reason: Run an audit-first hardening pass before declaring the new project production-ready.
phases.query_suffix: Run audit mode only unless the human has explicitly approved refactoring. Focus on the first-slice codebase, generated architecture, dependency risk, security, testability, and maintainability.

phases.name: Step 11 - Prepare release artifacts
phases.reason: Prepare changelog, version plan, release notes, and repository readiness summary without publishing unless explicitly approved.
phases.query_suffix: STOP BEFORE PUSHING TO GITHUB. Prepare local release artifacts, changelog entry, version plan, and readiness report, but do not push, tag, publish, or create a GitHub Release unless the human explicitly approves.

phases.name: Step 12 - Deliver project genesis summary
phases.reason: Summarize all generated artifacts, code, verification evidence, risks, and next decisions.
phases.query_suffix: Produce a concise final project genesis report with: project summary, artifact paths, repository path, implemented slice, validation evidence, release readiness, blocked items, and recommended next actions. Base every claim on prior phase evidence.
